qualification: local pinned-fixture reliability investigation; not hardware, cross-host, G1-G5, or release qualification

candidateChange.description: Publish exact Tier-one live-in and cumulative-dirty register masks while forcing the analysis helpers out of the already-large emitter body.
candidateChange.machineCodeEffect: The masks are side-table values and do not alter the compiled block's machineWords.
candidateChange.focusedVerification: 80 tests in the metadata and Tier-one suites passed.
candidateChange.aggregateVerification: The 1,545-test/179-suite aggregate passed twice after one non-reproducing concurrent-suite issue.

disposition.reason: One pass and one generated-code crash do not meet the production reliability gate.
disposition.safeState: Tier-one recovery masks remain conservative all-GPR values.
disposition.nextInvestigation: Treat the invalid generated return address as a layout-sensitive native chain, trace, predictor, or memory-prologue lifecycle defect; isolate it independently before re-enabling exact metadata.

limitations: The crash occurred before the runner could publish its terminal diagnostic receipt, so the exact guest instruction count and JIT counters for the failed run are unavailable.
The candidate's side-table values do not alter emitted guest machine words, so this evidence does not by itself prove that mask analysis caused the invalid return address.
The successful second run does not override the failed reliability result.
